government.note: Parliamentary monarchy under the Constitution of 1978. The Prime Minister (President of the Government) is invested by the Congress of Deputies and can be removed only by a constructive vote of no confidence (as happened to Mariano Rajoy on 1 June 2018). The monarch's role is largely ceremonial. A total revision of the Constitution, or a revision of its core titles, must be ratified by referendum; other amendments go to referendum only if a tenth of either chamber requests it. Consultative national referendums may also be called (the 2005 European Constitution referendum).

system.note: Closed-list proportional representation in 52 constituencies (the 50 provinces plus Ceuta and Melilla, which elect one deputy each by plurality), with a 3% threshold applied in each constituency rather than nationally. The 2000 general election was held on 12 March 2000, so seats_2000 is the composition of the chamber at its dissolution in January 2000 (6th Cortes, elected 3 March 1996). PSOE includes its Catalan partner PSC (19). The PP list of 1996 elected 153 PP, 2 UPN and 1 PAR deputies. United Left had won 21 seats in 1996, but the Democratic Party of the New Left (3) and Initiative for Catalonia-Greens (2) had left its group. 'others' is Pilar Rahola of the Partit per la Independència, elected for ERC in 1996. The Canarian Coalition's 4 deputies belonged to its member parties AIC (2), ICAN and CCN.

source.title: Wikipedia: 2000 Spanish general election (Outgoing parliament: composition in January 2000)

system.note: 208 senators were directly elected in 2000 by limited (partial block) vote, four per mainland province with each voter choosing up to three, with fixed numbers for the islands, Ceuta and Melilla; the rest are appointed by the regional legislatures in proportion to their population, so the size varies (259 at dissolution in January 2000; 267 seats, 209 of them elected, from the 2026 constitutional reform giving Formentera its own senator). seats_2000 is the composition at dissolution in January 2000. PSOE includes PSC (10). The Canarian Coalition's 2 are its member groups AIC and AHI. 'others' are one senator of the Pacte Progressista (Ibiza-Formentera) and one of the Lanzarote Independents Party. The Senate cannot bring down the government.
